title: Workflow Template
description: Versioned, declarative composition of role contracts stored under registry/workflows/*.yaml (spec §3.2, Appendix F, DESIGN.md §3). A workflow template performs composition only; it never encodes planning or architecture decisions (spec §3.2 conditional stages, F.0 failure modes).

version.description: Template version (spec §3.2). Missions and tasks pin this version.

description.description: Human-readable purpose of the workflow (spec §3.2 registry table).

entry_conditions.description: Conditions that must hold before this workflow may be instantiated (spec §3.2).

required_inputs.description: Artifact names/URIs the mission must supply (spec §3.2).

stages.description: Role/stage DAG (spec §3.2, F.0). The compiler validates every stage maps to a known role, dependencies are explicit and acyclic, all mission outputs are covered, and every human gate has a named DAG point (DESIGN.md §3).

required_outputs.description: Output artifact names the workflow's stages must jointly produce (spec §3.2).

terminal_condition.description: Mechanical condition marking the workflow complete (spec §3.2). Shape is workflow-specific: a short description string, or a structured predicate.

workflow.description: Workflow template id the child mission runs.

gated_by.description: Named human gate that must approve child-mission creation (spec §6.0: creating a child mission is a human gate by default).

child_missions.description: Child workflows this template may spawn (spec §3.2, §6.0).

stage.description: One DAG node (spec F.0 workflow_instance example). role is required for ordinary stages; a type: child-mission stage may omit role and instead carry gated_by directly, per the F.0 create-implementation-mission example.

depends_on.description: Ids of stages this stage depends on (spec F.0).

outputs.description: Artifact names/URIs this stage produces (spec F.0).

human_gate.description: Named human approval gate at this DAG point (spec §3.2, F.0).

gated_by.description: Named gate that must clear before a child-mission stage executes (spec F.0 create-implementation-mission example).

condition.description: Every conditional stage names either a mechanical predicate the compiler evaluates from policy, or an owning role that makes the judgment call (spec §3.2 Conditional stages).
